data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The single dominant cross-city modulator of the nocturnal UHI is the sky view factor: cities with deeper, denser street canyons have a smaller effective sky view, which suppresses longwave radiative cooling because emitted radiation is intercepted by facing walls rather than escaping to the cold sky, so the nighttime gap scales with building height and built density through their control of sky view.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the nocturnal UHI does not correlate with sky view factor across cities, the geometric mechanism is falsified","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If cities with tall buildings but wide streets show the same UHI as cities with short buildings, building height alone is not the driver","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If radiative flux measurements show that net longwave loss is similar in urban and rural areas, the trapping mechanism is negligible","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the UHI is larger in cities with high sky view but high thermal mass, sky view is not the dominant modulator","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Nocturnal cooling in both urban and rural environments is primarily driven by net longwave radiative flux to the sky. In the countryside, the sky view factor is near unity, so surfaces radiate efficiently to the cold atmospheric sink. In cities, buildings partially obscure the sky, reducing the effective sky view factor. Radiation from street surfaces is intercepted by building walls, which re-radiate part of it back, creating a radiative trapping effect. This slows the urban cooling rate. Cities with taller buildings and narrower streets have a smaller sky view factor, so radiative cooling is more strongly suppressed, producing a larger nocturnal UHI. The thermal storage of building walls amplifies this by providing a warm radiative source facing the street.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
